parts.stem: The proton ($^{1}\text{H}$) NMR spectrum of atorvastatin dissolved in $\text{CDCl}_{3}$ is recorded.
parts.text: Use Table 5.1 to deduce the number of hydrogen atoms that could produce peaks in the region $\delta = 6.5-13.0\text{ ppm}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.stem: The proton ($^{1}\text{H}$) NMR spectrum of atorvastatin dissolved in $\text{D}_{2}\text{O}$ is recorded.
parts.text:
Predict the number of hydrogen atoms that would not show a peak in this spectrum.

Explain your answer.

Table 5.1

| environment of proton | example | chemical shift range $\delta / \text{ppm}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| alkane | $-\text{CH}_{3}$, $-\text{CH}_{2}-$, $>\text{CH}-$ | 0.9-1.7 |
| alkyl next to C=O | $\text{CH}_{3}-\text{C=O}$, $-\text{CH}_{2}-\text{C=O}$, $>\text{CH}-\text{C=O}$ | 2.2-3.0 |
| alkyl next to aromatic ring | $\text{CH}_{3}-\text{Ar}$, $-\text{CH}_{2}-\text{Ar}$, $>\text{CH}-\text{Ar}$ | 2.3-3.0 |
| alkyl next to electronegative atom | $\text{CH}_{3}-\text{O}$, $-\text{CH}_{2}-\text{O}$, $-\text{CH}_{2}-\text{Cl}$ | 3.2-4.0 |
| attached to alkene | $=\text{CHR}$ | 4.5-6.0 |
| attached to aromatic ring | $\text{H}-\text{Ar}$ | 6.0-9.0 |
| aldehyde | $\text{HCOR}$ | 9.3-10.5 |
| alcohol | $\text{ROH}$ | 0.5-6.0 |
| phenol | $\text{Ar}-\text{OH}$ | 4.5-7.0 |
| carboxylic acid | $\text{RCOOH}$ | 9.0-13.0 |
| alkyl amine | $\text{R}-\text{NH}-$ | 1.0-5.0 |
| aryl amine | $\text{Ar}-\text{NH}_{2}$ | 3.0-6.0 |
| amide | $\text{RCONHR}$ | 5.0-12.0 |
